newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong air cargo bottleneck seen for Q4 peak.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong air cargo bottleneck seen for Q4 peak.

text.p: Air cargo capacity from Hong Kong to North America is becoming hard to find and traffic backlogs are beginning to develop, a leading U.S. freight forwarder official told Reuters.

Barry Richard, director of pricing for Expeditors International, said in a telephone interview that forwarders and consolidators are scrambling to line up lift for the balance of the fourth quarter peak, with most Asian gateways tight on space.
Richard said Expeditors has been making use of extra freighter sections offered by Air China, but sees little uncommitted space in the market over the next several weeks.
Expeditors, he said, has even tried to ship some U.S.-destined freight from Hong Kong via Europe, but those corridors are tight on space as well.

He emphasized that the situation is not necessarily worse than a typical fourth quarter peak in the ex-Asia market, but it is quite a bit busier than the fourth quarter last year when demand for ex-Asia capacity slumped.
"This year we have a peak," he said. "Last year, we didn't have a peak". -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
